message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value (standard conditions) | Notes |
|----------|-----------------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.008 u (average) | Weighted average of its three stable isotopes. |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (^2H, 0.02 %) – stable; Tritium (^3H) – radioactive, half‑life ≈ 12.32 y. | Deuterium used in heavy water; tritium in nuclear fusion research. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | One valence electron → highly reactive. |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | Highest of all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | Negative value indicates energy release when gaining an electron. |
| **Molecular form** | H₂ (diatomic) | Most common state at ambient conditions. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) | Extremely low; vaporizes easily. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (–434.69 °F) | Sublimes at atmospheric pressure. |
| **Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Lightest gas. |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 14.304 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | High relative to its molar mass. |
| **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (combustion). | Forms hydrides with many metals. |
| **Bonding behavior** | Forms covalent bonds (H–H, H–C, H–O, etc.). | Can act as a proton donor (acidic). |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (H⁺ donor) in aqueous solution. | In organic chemistry, behaves as a nucleophile or electrophile depending on context. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). | Fundamental to astrophysics and spectroscopy. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), metallurgy (reducing agent), semiconductor manufacturing, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents), etc. | Also used in isotope labeling studies. |

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Both atomic and molecular forms are extremely light.
- **Highly reactive**: One valence electron makes it eager to share or donate electrons.
- **Strong ionization energy & electronegativity**: Requires significant energy to remove its lone electron.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (most abundant), deuterium (stable heavy isotope), tritium (radioactive, used in fusion).
- **Key role in chemistry & physics**: From forming the simplest covalent bond (H₂) to being the cornerstone of stellar nucleosynthesis and modern energy technologies.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
